findings: Frozen39e evaluation reproduces original metrics exactly on both development and stress. Base control reproduces56/72. Wide improves descriptive case count but strict width contrast fails its median-effect and worst-seed guards.

Ten timing failures: Im same_v_history case0 seed43 offset0.4ms; K_Pst slow_recovery case0 all seeds offset2.0/2.6/4.8ms; Nap_Et2 slow_recovery case1 all seeds offset13.0/11.2/1.2ms; Nap_Et2 calcium_switch case0 all seeds peak1.2ms. Two current RMSE failures: SK_E2 reversal case0 seed17 normalized0.0134423; K_Tst activation_boundary case0 seed29 normalized0.0155954.

Temporal treatment collapses to0-2/72 with finite parameters. At120k base_t1_s0 temporal gradient norm is239.5/73.4/473.1 times the combined other gradient across seeds. These are sampled FIT probes, not a causal intervention.

Fixed temporal weights49.88-56.75 are calibrated on initial FIT gradients. Temporal precision term is bounded by tanh but derivative term is unbounded. Band weights are0.5-1, so off-event flat regions still contribute. Window baseline and10% excursion are local to6.4ms chunks, unlike full-trajectory evaluation. These are source-code facts, not proof of the cause of failure.

Frozen39e oracle: learned56;teacher_u62;teacher_z61;both72. Timing failures10->9 with teacher_u and10->5 with teacher_z. FP64 alone remains56. Repeat these interventions on39f before attributing new residuals to the same cause.

Recovery sampling changes windows in the same FIT/FIT_EXTRA corpus; it does not test independent data expansion. Held anchors supervise long constant-input composition, but variable-input backpropagation spans64ticks=6.4ms. Therefore short temporal credit assignment remains a candidate even with long held anchors.

All72 gate checks pass in best model, yet timing fails. Broader network improves current error but does not resolve timing. Resident-core speed is7.87-7.89x, versus8.01-8.03x base; no end-to-end or quality-qualified speed claim.

hypotheses.statement: Fixed initial weighting lets the temporal auxiliary dominate later learning and interfere with the accurate trajectory/coefficient solution.
hypotheses.test: Same frozen39f initialization: original temporal weight versus0.01x versus no temporal term; matched batches, optimizer reset, budget, selection. Record weighted gradient norms, cosines and clipping at every checkpoint.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reducing the multiplier demonstrably restores gradient balance but does not recover primary quality or timing over matched controls; dominance is then insufficient as explanation.

hypotheses.statement: Derivative penalty and/or slope-conditioned precision on flat/off-event regions create harmful learning pressure; the local window proxy is misaligned with full event timing.
hypotheses.test: 2x2 old full/precision-only by full/0.01 weight plus no-aux control; then matched low-weight event-aligned surrogate using full FIT-episode baseline/threshold metadata and explicit masks for unevaluable events. Probe precision and derivative gradients separately, tanh saturation and inverse-slope distribution. Test constant offset, known time shift, flat trace, reversal and repeated excursions synthetically.
hypotheses.falsifier: Neither component removal nor event alignment improves matched results despite passing toy sensitivity and gradient tests; proxy anatomy is then not sufficient.

hypotheses.statement: 6.4ms variable-input training and teacher initialization at each window underconstrain long recovery timing, even with long held-input anchors.
hypotheses.test: 2x2 no-aux/event-aligned by64/256-tick recurrence, identical512 target ticks per update and same source pool. Retain separate held-anchor objective. Measure long-window gradients and full free state recurrence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Longer recurrence at equal target exposure provides no paired timing improvement or coefficient-drift reduction; test budget dependence before rejecting all horizon effects.

hypotheses.statement: Small learned rate and equilibrium biases accumulate into large offsets on shallow tails; rate error is a major but non-exclusive contributor.
hypotheses.test: On frozen39f winner evaluate learned,u-only,z-only,both and teacher-state-reset in FP32/64; record signed crossings and individual channel trajectories. Oracles remain nonselectable and do not restore formulas in deployed candidate.
hypotheses.falsifier: Replacing both coefficients fails the reference floor or errors remain with teacher-state reset; investigate evaluation/readout contract before further training.

hypotheses.statement: Rare transitions and recovery tails remain underrepresented in the existing FIT corpus; resampling cannot create missing variation.
hypotheses.test: For both long-window no-aux and aligned-loss arms compare existing corpus against additional independent FIT seeds/protocol parameters generated by a preregistered regime grid, matched update and target budgets. Do not copy failing development trajectories. Use multiple budget checkpoints to distinguish support from optimization.
hypotheses.falsifier: Verified support expansion across the intended regimes yields no paired gains at adequate measured optimization budgets; data insufficiency becomes less plausible within that tested scope.

hypotheses.priority: low for pureFP32; open for new winner event conditioning
hypotheses.statement: Shallow slopes or near-degenerate peaks amplify tiny waveform discrepancies; part of residual timing may be poorly conditioned, while acceptance must still enforce the registered metric.
hypotheses.test: Frozen39f FP64, tiny perturbation, connected-excursion identity and quarter-grid phase probes; report raw traces and linear crossing-shift approximation. Existing metric remains primary unchanged.
hypotheses.falsifier: Events remain uniquely identified and stable to probes while large timing shifts persist; metric conditioning/precision alone cannot explain those failures.
